data.text: The sellers table already has a `seller_state` column with two-letter Brazilian state codes. I don't need to join with geolocation - I can directly count sellers by state. Let me run the SQL query to get the top 10 states by seller count.

args.purpose: Count distinct sellers per state and get top 10
args.sql:
SELECT 
    seller_state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) as seller_count
FROM sellers
GROUP BY seller_state
ORDER BY seller_count DESC
LIMIT 10

data.sql:
SELECT 
    seller_state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) as seller_count
FROM sellers
GROUP BY seller_state
ORDER BY seller_count DESC

| Rank | State | Seller Count |

| 1 | SP (São Paulo) | 1,849 |

| 10 | BA (Bahia) | 19 |

The data shows a clear concentration of sellers in the Southeast region, with São Paulo (SP) dominating with 1,849 sellers - more than five times the next state. The remaining states have significantly fewer sellers, ranging from 349 down to 19.
